listing.name: The Catacomb Apocalypse (ReflectionHLE)
listing.summary: Use The Catacomb Apocalypse with its upstream ReflectionHLE Windows player and your own matching original game files. Setup and updates stay upstream-owned.

steps.title: Use the matching original DOS edition
steps.instruction: Use your complete matching DOS Apocalypse folder, including APOCGAME.EXE, AUDIO.APC, EGAGRAPH.APC, GAMEMAPS.APC and the required SHP companion files. Abyss shareware does not supply Apocalypse. The ReflectionHLE launcher lists the exact supported versions and required files. Select the real original folder there; its executable is original input, not the Windows player to register. Reuse a recognized installed copy without moving your originals.

steps.title: Register the upstream Windows player
steps.instruction: Extract the official Windows 64-bit ZIP and keep reflectionhle.exe, SDL3.dll and libspeexdsp-1.dll together. Select reflectionhle.exe inside its wrapper folder and use that same folder as the working directory. Leave launch arguments empty to use the game/version picker. Complete original-file selection in the upstream launcher after explicit Play. Registration does not start it; Portcove discovery runs no original EXE, helper or game.

steps.title: Preserve the shared profile and each game version
steps.instruction: Windows normally stores ReflectionHLE settings and per-version writable data beneath %APPDATA%/reflectionhle. Preserve that whole profile, your original game folders and any custom data/config/mod locations with all copies closed before changing runtimes. Several game entries share settings; version-specific writable folders remain distinct. Changing a data/config argument redirects storage and does not migrate it. Retain the working runtime for existing saves; no cross-version or cross-engine save compatibility is established.

steps.title: Keep upstream update ownership
steps.instruction: You and upstream maintain this external player, original files and profile. Portcove offers explicit registration, supervised Play and registration-only removal; it does not acquire ownership of the external files or offer managed Update, Backup, Rollback or deletion. Keep a working copy and back up its actual data before an upstream update. Other platforms need their own supported upstream package/application flow; this Windows guide does not establish native execution on any platform.
